title: The Stadium Has the Last Word
title_candidates: The Stadium Has the Last Word
Four Rounds, Three Verdicts, One Course
theme: The best golf of the week arrives on the last day and wins only the Jacket, while the Trophy is carried off by a man going backwards down the closing stretch.
opening_hook: Gregg Williams played the round of the week on the one afternoon it could not change the Trophy, and the Stadium's closing four holes took their money from everybody else.

round_story.subject: Gregg Williams's closing 44 points and 84 gross at the Stadium — the best round of the day by six points and by six shots gross — sealing the TEG 18 Green Jacket
round_story.why_it_matters: It was the best round of the final day on both measures, it set a new personal best for Williams at PGA Catalunya - Stadium, and it turned a Green Jacket lead of eight into a 14-shot procession.
round_story.shape: Williams began the day eight clear of David Mullin in the Jacket and nine adrift of nobody in particular in the Trophy, having trailed the Trophy lead by as much as 15 during the week. A birdie at the short 5th and a par-bogey-par run through the 8th, 9th and 10th — nine points in three holes, on the course's stroke index 1 among them — built a round nobody else came close to. He signed for 44 points and 84 gross: 12 over par, six better than anyone else in the field, and one stroke better than his own previous best at this course, set earlier in the same TEG.
headline_candidates: Forty-Four Points and a Course Best
round_story.chosen_headline: Forty-Four Points and a Course Best
round_story.standfirst: Williams's 84 gross is his lowest score in seven visits to the Stadium, and his third-best gross round in 67 TEG rounds.

race_story.subject: Alex Baker wins the TEG 18 Trophy on 169 by eight from John Patterson despite a 10 and an 8 in the final round, while finishing bottom of the Green Jacket table
race_story.why_it_matters: This is the coronation: the Trophy is decided, and it is decided by a man whose final round included the worst hole of the week and the worst gross score in the field.
race_story.shape: Alex Baker began the last day 12 clear of John Patterson and never looked like losing it, having led since the first afternoon. Then came the 14th — a sextuple-bogey 10, no points — followed by a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 17th, part of a closing stretch that also cost him seven gross shots across the 9th, 10th and 11th; Patterson's 42 points, built on nine points through the 4th, 5th and 6th, clawed back four of the twelve and no more. Alex Baker signed for 38 points, 169 in total and the Trophy by eight, and simultaneously slid from second after round one to fifth and last in the Jacket on 124.
headline_candidates: A Ten an Eight and the Trophy
race_story.standfirst: John Patterson outplayed him over two of the four rounds and still finished eight adrift.

discovered_storylines.subject: Jon Baker takes the TEG 18 Wooden Spoon by 23 shots after five consecutive double bogeys from the 7th to the 11th
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The Spoon was settled long before Tuesday, but the manner of it — five doubles in a row, last in the field for the third time in four rounds — is the week in miniature.
discovered_storylines.shape: Jon Baker arrived at the Stadium already 14 adrift at the bottom of the Trophy table and needing only to survive. Instead he posted a double bogey at the 7th, then at the 8th, then the 9th, then the 10th, then the 11th — five in a row, ten gross shots gone, a single point apiece — before finally breaking a twelve-hole run without a par with a birdie at the 13th. A round of 29 points left him on 126, 23 behind David Mullin and in sole possession of the Spoon.
headline_candidates: Five Straight Doubles Settle the Spoon
Ten Shots Gone in Five Holes
A Birdie Arrives Far Too Late
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Five Straight Doubles Settle the Spoon
discovered_storylines.standfirst: The birdie at the 13th ended a run of twelve holes without a par, by which point the arithmetic had long since stopped mattering.

discovered_storylines.subject: The Stadium's closing stretch, holes 14 to 17, which took shots off almost everyone in the field on the final afternoon
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The same four holes that ended Alex Baker's scorecard hospitality also gutted David Mullin's round and nearly ruined John Patterson's, which is a course doing the work rather than any one player failing.
discovered_storylines.shape: David Mullin reached the 14th with a respectable round in hand and left the 17th nine gross shots worse off — double, triple, double, double, four holes without a net par. John Patterson took a triple at the 14th and a double at the 15th before a bogey at the 16th steadied him and a birdie at the 17th stopped the bleeding altogether. Only Gregg Williams and the scorer's pencil emerged from the stretch intact.
headline_candidates: The Stadium Collects Its Debts Late
Nine Shots Gone in Four Holes
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Spain's premier championship course saved its teeth for the last hour of TEG 18.

race_state_note: Gregg Williams's 44 lifted him to third in the Trophy on 160, one behind John Patterson and nine behind Alex Baker, having trailed the lead by as much as 15 during the week; the Trophy lead narrowed from 12 to 8 but was never genuinely in danger, and the Jacket and Spoon both widened.
